highlights: Each finished crucible yields 1 glass pane. Two panes require 4 sand and 3 sticks; sand is dug at the Glassworks, so a nearby warehouse does not remove that work.

Each hot crucible cools for 80 simulation seconds (0.267 game day). There are two cooling positions: their combined ceiling is 7.5 panes per day if kept occupied continuously. Filling and emptying them, shared oven access and the workday reduce actual output.
The one-worker model is about 5.9 panes per day; the two-worker model reaches the cooling ceiling of 7.5, rather than doubling. These are supplied-capacity estimates, not measured yields.
105728.name: Glassworks

highlights: One cheese wheel is cut into 6 portions of cheese. The material balance of 12 cheese per stick combines two batches; it is not the yield of one wheel.

Milking the building’s cows is part of the production process. The model includes the milking action, stirring, unmolding, cutting and fuel preparation. It excludes travel to the cow and equipment changes.

Aging takes 400 simulation seconds (1⅓ game days) per wheel, with six aging positions. Fully occupied, those positions have a ceiling of 27 cheese portions per day. More workers do not shorten aging. Cow availability, handoffs and work schedules can leave positions empty.
